sections.content: If you are searching for real estate deals in Killeen TX, you have landed on one of the most underrated investor markets in the entire Lone Star State. Killeen sits in Central Texas, just outside Fort Cavazos — one of the largest military installations in the world — and that single fact drives a steady, predictable demand for housing that most markets simply cannot match. Whether you are a first-time investor just getting your feet wet (check out this [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before you dive in) or a seasoned wholesaler looking to diversify your deal flow, Killeen deserves a serious look.
Killeen TX Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Killeen is a city of roughly 160,000 people in Bell County, Texas. The city's economy is almost entirely anchored by Fort Cavazos, which employs over 40,000 active-duty soldiers and tens of thousands of civilian contractors. That workforce creates a near-constant pipeline of renters and buyers moving in and out of the area on military orders, typically every two to three years. This cycle is a goldmine for real estate investors because demand rarely dips. Even during national housing slowdowns, Killeen tends to hold steady because military families need housing regardless of what the broader economy is doing.

The Killeen-Temple metro area has also seen consistent population growth over the past decade, adding retail, healthcare, and logistics jobs that extend the renter pool well beyond just military families. For a full picture of current inventory, pricing, and deal flow in this market, visit our [Killeen TX market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/killeen-tx) for up-to-date data.
Average Home Prices in Killeen TX

One of the biggest draws for investors is Killeen's affordability. As of mid-2024, the median home price in Killeen sits around $185,000 to $210,000, depending on the neighborhood and condition. That is significantly below the Texas state median of roughly $300,000, which means lower entry costs, smaller loans, and faster paths to positive cash flow. Distressed properties — the kind wholesalers and flippers target — often surface in the $90,000 to $140,000 range, leaving plenty of room for profit after repairs and resale.

Pro Tip: Before making any offer in Killeen, run your numbers through the free [ARV Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator). Knowing your after-repair value before you negotiate is one of the fastest ways to avoid overpaying on a deal.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Killeen TX

Not all zip codes in Killeen are created equal. Investors should focus their energy on neighborhoods with strong rental demand, reasonable property taxes, and clear comps for after-repair values. Here are the areas that consistently produce the best results.
Top Investor-Friendly Areas

items: Trimmier Estates & North Killeen: Older housing stock, lots of distressed inventory, and high rental demand from enlisted soldiers. Great for wholesalers and buy-and-hold investors.
Clearwater / Yowell Ranch: Newer subdivisions with strong resale comps. Best for fix-and-flip investors who want cleaner rehabs and faster exits.
Nolan Ranch & Monterra Village: Mid-range neighborhoods popular with NCOs and civilian contractors. Solid rental yields and lower vacancy rates.
Killeen East (near Rancier Ave corridor): Higher crime perception keeps prices low, but savvy investors who know the block-by-block dynamics can find strong cash-flowing rentals here.
Harker Heights (adjacent suburb): Slightly higher price points but also higher rents and a more stable long-term tenant base. Worth including in your search radius.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Killeen TX
Wholesale Deals

Killeen is a fantastic wholesale market. The constant military turnover means motivated sellers are always around — soldiers who get PCS orders and need to sell fast, families dealing with foreclosure after a deployment disruption, or inherited properties from out-of-state heirs who just want to close quickly. The key to locking up wholesale deals here is direct-to-seller marketing: driving for dollars in North Killeen, sending targeted direct mail to pre-foreclosure lists, or pulling absentee owner data. If you are new to this strategy, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) to build your outreach system from scratch. Assignment fees in Killeen typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 per deal, depending on the ARV and the depth of the discount you negotiate.
Fix and Flip

Flipping in Killeen works best when you stick to neighborhoods with clear, recent sold comps and avoid areas where ARVs are difficult to pin down. A typical Killeen flip might look like this: buy a 3-bedroom, 2-bath home in Clearwater for $130,000, invest $35,000 in cosmetic and mechanical repairs, and resell for $205,000. That leaves a gross profit of roughly $40,000 before holding costs and agent fees — a solid margin for a market this affordable. The flip cycle in Killeen is usually 90 to 120 days from purchase to sale, which keeps your capital moving.
Rental Properties and Buy-and-Hold

Long-term rentals are arguably where Killeen shines the brightest. A 3-bedroom home purchased for $170,000 can rent for $1,300 to $1,600 per month in most neighborhoods. Run those numbers and you are looking at a gross rent multiplier under 12 — a metric most investors in Austin or Dallas can only dream about. Military tenants, especially those receiving a Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH), are often considered among the most reliable renters in any market because their housing stipend is tied to their paycheck and rank. Many landlords in Killeen report vacancy rates below 5% year over year.

"Military markets like Killeen are recession-resistant by design. When the rest of the country slows down, Fort Cavazos keeps running — and those soldiers still need a place to live." — Common wisdom among Central Texas real estate investors
Local Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Rising insurance costs are squeezing margins slightly, so factor in 15-20% higher property insurance quotes compared to 2022 when underwriting your deals.

Interest rate sensitivity: Killeen buyers are more rate-sensitive than buyers in luxury markets. Higher rates in 2023-2024 have kept some first-time buyers renting longer, which is actually good news for landlords.

New construction competition: Several national builders are active in Harker Heights and Nolanville. This puts a ceiling on ARVs in some areas, so verify your comps are not being skewed by builder incentives.

Short-term rental growth: Killeen is not a typical Airbnb market, but mid-term rentals (30-90 days) targeting soldiers in transition, contractors on assignment, and traveling nurses at the Killeen VA have become a profitable niche.
Property tax stabilization: Bell County has seen property tax assessments level off after the big jumps of 2021-2022, which improves long-term cash flow projections for buy-and-hold investors.

sections.content: Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Killeen TX

Killeen attracts a growing number of remote investors, and for good reason — the price points are low enough that a single deal can be analyzed, contracted, and closed without ever stepping on a plane. That said, investing from a distance requires a tighter system. Here is what experienced remote investors do differently in this market.

items: Build a local boots-on-the-ground team first: Find a property manager, a licensed inspector, and a rehab contractor before you make your first offer. Facebook groups for Killeen real estate investors are a great starting point.

Use virtual wholesalers and local bird dogs: Killeen has an active wholesale community. Partnering with a local wholesaler who already has deal flow can get you into properties faster than building your own pipeline from scratch.

Understand military lease protections: The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) gives active-duty tenants the right to break leases under certain conditions. This is not a deal-breaker, but you need to understand it before you become a landlord here.

Verify neighborhood-level data: Killeen's investment quality can change dramatically block by block. Use satellite images, street view tools, and local property managers to validate any deal before committing.

Learn to analyze deals fast: Remote investing rewards investors who can underwrite quickly and decisively. Study up on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) so you never miss a good deal because the numbers took too long to run.

Is Killeen TX Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Killeen is not a glamorous market. It will not show up in flashy magazine articles about the hottest cities in America. But for investors who prioritize cash flow over appreciation, steady demand over speculation, and affordability over prestige, it checks nearly every box. The combination of a military-anchored economy, low median home prices, strong rental yields, and an active wholesale community makes it one of the most reliable markets in Central Texas for generating real, repeatable profits. Whether you are looking for your first deal or your fiftieth, the fundamentals here are hard to argue with.
